claims.text: Superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloys is primarily governed by atomic disorder arising from high mixing entropy.
Atomic disorder modulates electron–phonon coupling through softening of local vibrational modes.
(TaNb)1–x(ZrHfTi)x is an example of the relevant high-entropy-alloy system.
The proposed initial alloy is homogeneous, single-phase, and highly chemically disordered.
Equiatomic, compositionally diverse alloys have higher mixing entropy than comparable alloys with fewer principal elements or non-equiatomic ratios.
Superconducting measurements can be conducted at temperatures of at least 1.8 K.
An inert atmosphere avoids oxidation during the proposed experiments.
Identical sample preparation will keep microstructural features comparable apart from mixing entropy.
Atomic-scale disorder and local variations in the phonon spectrum mediate changes in electron–phonon coupling.
Increased compositional complexity enhances atomic disorder.
Enhanced atomic disorder broadens and softens vibrational modes.
Broadening and softening of vibrational modes enhance electron–phonon coupling.
Changes in electron–phonon coupling affect Tc and the critical magnetic fields.
Higher-mixing-entropy samples will have a higher Tc than compositionally similar lower-entropy alloys.
Higher-mixing-entropy samples will have altered critical fields relative to lower-entropy controls.
The disorder-mediated mechanism is expected to dominate only in single-phase, homogeneously mixed alloys without segregation, secondary phases, or oxidation.
The proposed mechanism is relevant when superconducting pairing is primarily phonon-mediated.
Prior studies of (TaNb)1–x(ZrHfTi)x report composition-dependent superconducting properties, including Tc up to 7 K and a critical field around 10 T at different mixing ratios.
VSM-SQUID magnetometry can determine Tc, Hc1, and Hc2 in these HEA samples.
The hypothesis is falsified if the high-entropy samples show neither a statistically significant Tc increase or critical-field alteration nor the expected vibrational-mode changes.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as already having demonstrably lower Tc and/or different critical fields, which partly preselects the predicted outcome and conflicts with using absence of those differences as an open falsification result.
